title: Count Routes to Climb a Rectangular Grid
summary: Given a string array grid of size n, where each string grid[i] has length m, and each character grid[i][j] is either '.' (available cell) or '#' (blocked cell), count the number of distinct routes from any cell in the bottom row (row n - 1) to any cell in the top row (row 0).
statement: Given a string array grid of size n, where each string grid[i] has length m, and each character grid[i][j] is either '.' (available cell) or '#' (blocked cell), count the number of distinct routes from any cell in the bottom row (row n - 1) to any cell in the top row (row 0). Each move must be to an available cell and must not exceed a Euclidean distance of d, where d is a given integer. Moves can only be to the row directly above, and you cannot stay on the same row for two consecutive moves. The result should be returned modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: grid has at most 750 rows and columns; dots are available and hashes blocked.
A move stays on its row or goes one row up, with Euclidean distance at most d.
At most one consecutive same-row move is allowed; routes start on the bottom and end on the top.
reference_solution:
def count_grid_climbing_routes(grid,d):
    from math import isqrt
    mod=1000000007;n=len(grid);m=len(grid[0])
    def window(values,radius):
        prefix=[0]
        for value in values:prefix.append((prefix[-1]+value)%mod)
        return [(prefix[min(m,i+radius+1)]-prefix[max(0,i-radius)])%mod for i in range(m)]
    first=[1 if grid[-1][col]=='.' else 0 for col in range(m)]
    vertical=isqrt(d*d-1)
    for row in range(n-1,-1,-1):
        nearby=window(first,d)
        second=[(nearby[col]-first[col])%mod if grid[row][col]=='.' else 0 for col in range(m)]
        total=[(first[col]+second[col])%mod for col in range(m)]
        if row==0:return sum(total)%mod
        upward=window(total,vertical)
        first=[upward[col] if grid[row-1][col]=='.' else 0 for col in range(m)]

hints: Within each row, distinguish arriving/starting at a first hold from taking the optional second hold.
Prefix-sum windows count horizontal destinations within d; subtract the same cell because a move must change cells.
Combine one- and two-hold routes, then move upward using horizontal radius floor(sqrt(d²-1)).
These two states enforce at most one horizontal move per row, and every legal route has a unique sequence of first and optional second holds.
